title.narrative: Strengthening the Environmental Performance Monitoring & Evaluation System of the Phil Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) system

description.narrative: " PD 1586 promulgated the Phil Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Law in 1977. Several implementing tules and regulations were passed through the years, the most comprehensive of which is DO No. 96-37 issued in 1996 and DO No. 2000-5 issued in 2000. Environmental Compliance Certificates (ECCs) are issued to proposed projects having adequate mitigating measures to address potential environmental impacts. The ECC also serves as a legal instrument that binds the proponent to carry out an impact reduction/environmental enhancement program during the operational life of a project. As a planning and analytical tool, the Philippine Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) System has evolved to become one of the most powerful regulatory instruments to ensure sustainable development in the country. An important objective oaf the CAS for Philippines is to ensure environmentally sustainable urban and rural development and increase support to environmental protection programs. Fundamentally, the Bank's supportr to the GOP aims at fostering not just a steady pace of economic gtrowth but also emphasizes the need to address the links between poverty, environment and sustainability. An ongoing study for the Philippines entitled ""Environmental Safegaurds Risk Assessment"" identified at least 70% of the 12 Category A & B projects in the portfolio as having marginal to risky safeguards performance, with GOP's almost non-existent monitoring of compliance to environmental covenants. This proposal outlines a capacity building initiative which would support those primary objectives of Bank assistance to the GOP. The proposed assitance has 2 over-arching objectives. First, it will strengthen the ability of the environmenatal regulatory agencies, LGUs and local communities to monitor, evaluate and report compliance to environmental covenants and regulations including the implementation of environmental management and mitigation plans (EMPs), especially the World Bank supported projects. Second, it will improve GOP's capacity to develop and adopt innovative financial mechanisms and participatory approaches that will ensure the continued implementation of EMPs and compliance to ECCs even beyond the project life cycle."
